steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Monetary policy uses interest rates and money supply to influence the economy, primarily to control inflation (Bank of England's 2% CPI target).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Raising interest rates: reduces borrowing and spending, cools demand, lowers inflation, but may reduce growth and increase unemployment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lowering interest rates: stimulates borrowing and spending, boosts growth, but may cause inflation if demand exceeds supply.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Bank of England's MPC sets the base rate monthly, independently from government. Independence prevents politicians setting rates for electoral gain.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how the Bank of England could use monetary policy to reduce inflation. | Describe how lower interest rates might help reduce unemployment. | Evaluate whether monetary policy or fiscal policy is more effective at managing the economy.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: To reduce inflation, the Bank raises the base rate. This increases borrowing costs, reducing consumer spending. Higher saving rates encourage depositing rather than spending. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: The Bank of England sets interest rates INDEPENDENTLY from government. Always explain the TRANSMISSION MECHANISM: rate change -> borrowing costs -> spending -> demand -> inflation. When rates are near 0%, the Bank uses quantitative easing.
